To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Volvox genome has a high level of repetitive sequences, that these repetitive sequences are highly polymorphic, that the repetitive sequences can be used to map genes on the genome, that the repetitive elements are dispersed throughout the genome and are not clustered in the centromeric regions, and that the repetitive sequences are conserved between Volvox and Chlamydomonas.

the two distinct types of cells in Volvox are determined in early embryogenesis by two distinct pathways, and that the germ cell pathway is controlled by a single gene that encodes a transcription factor.

the Volvox germ plasm is composed of three distinct types of DNA molecules, that these molecules are not randomly dispersed throughout the germ line, and that the germ line contains at least three different types of chromosomes, each of which is composed of a unique combination of these DNA molecules.
